passages.text: In this paper, we propose Sparse-Scale Multi-Head Attention (SS-MHA), an optimized self-attention variant tailored for scientific literature.
By dynamically pruning low-entropy attention weights, our mechanism reduces memory overhead by 38.4% while improving ROUGE-L by 2.7 points.
Our chunking window uses size 600 characters with an overlap of 120 characters to preserve cross-sentence contextual continuity.
Experiments were executed on an Intel Core i7 machine with 16GB RAM using CPU-only inference to reflect student workstation constraints.
Dense Sentence-Transformers achieved an MRR of 0.812 compared to 0.548 for TF-IDF on technical passage retrieval.
